decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker: 'saving begins from a prominent address box at the top' + save produces title/description/website. Round 4 client: 'a clear address box up top where I paste a link and it fills in the details on its own.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Save-by-url conforms to REF-BM-01.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker positively enumerates collected/shown fields: 'each bookmark shows its title, short description, and website'. Round 4 client confirms only 'the real title ... a plain-language description ... and the website name (seriouseats.com)'. Favicon and preview image never presented or requested across the session.
decisions.note: Prototype review. REF-BM-02 requires auto-collecting favicon AND preview image; presented collection scope covers title/description/website only. The client approved without identifying the missing favicon/preview, so the difference passed unexpressed. (Title/description collection itself conforms.)

decisions.evidence: Rounds 6-7 inline edit of title/description after save; round 26 metadata-unavailable case lets the user supply a title before saving. Round 7 client: 'I make the fix inline, hit Save changes, and the bookmark comes right back showing my new description.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Editing auto-collected title/description before/after saving is realized; conforms (edit-after-save is a functionally equivalent path).

decisions.evidence: Round 6 maker assumption: correction edits 'only the title and description ... not the website name'. Round 6 client: 'I'd still expect, somewhere down the line, to be able to fix the actual link itself ... I don't want editing the address to fall off the list entirely.' Linked disposition rounds 41-42: maker 'Address correction would remain the later-cycle request we recorded'; round 42 client 'I'm comfortable with changing a bookmark's stored address being held for a later cycle.'
decisions.note: Prototype review + specification gate. REF-BM-04 includes editing the url; the edit flow excludes it. Client requested the missing reference requirement (extend) and it was recorded, then deferred to a later cycle with the client's agreement. One decision spanning rounds 6->41->42; capture is the requirement request, deferral does not negate it.

decisions.evidence: Round 27 maker: 'warns you that the page is already saved—and showing the existing bookmark instead of creating a duplicate'. Round 27 client: 'it warns me the page is already saved and shows me the one that's already in my library — so I end up back at the existing bookmark rather than cluttering things.'
decisions.note: Implementation/edge-case review. Duplicate-url converges to the existing bookmark; functionally equivalent to 'guide to edit existing'. Conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 23 maker: clicking the bookmark opens original page in a new tab, 'the whole bookmark card is clickable'. Round 23 client: 'Clicking the bookmark opens its original page in a new browser tab.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Selecting an item navigates to the original url; conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 29 maker: 'Travel — Create new tag' explicit creation in place. Round 29 client accepts creating a new tag when no match exists.
decisions.note: Prototype review. Assigning/creating tags conforms to REF-BM-09.

decisions.evidence: Round 9 maker offers Version A (inline type-to-suggest), B (chips to click), C (popover). Round 9 client: 'Version B just laid the tags out as chips to click, which is pleasant but I'd want the type-to-find as the collection grows. So A is my pick.' Round 10 confirms typing 'rec' surfaces existing 'Recipes'.
decisions.note: Prototype review, offered-alternatives select. The alternatives differ in fulfilment of REF-BM-10 (autocomplete): Version B provides no type-to-suggest. Offered decision marked diverged=true; client selected a reference-conforming alternative (A) and explicitly identified B's shortfall. catch_type=select.

decisions.evidence: Round 12 maker: filter to only 'Recipes' via sidebar tag list with active tag and result count. Round 12 client: 'click "Recipes" to narrow down ... clearly shows "Recipes" as the active tag with "2 bookmarks" as the count.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Tag filtering conforms; sidebar vs chip vs dropdown are functionally equivalent UI (client called it a preference).

decisions.evidence: Rounds 14-16 demonstrate matches on note, title, and description. Round 17 maker scopes search as 'live search across titles, descriptions, and your notes'; round 17 client repeats the same three fields. url as a searchable field is never presented, demonstrated, or requested.
decisions.note: Prototype review. REF-BM-12 requires full-text search over title, description, note, AND url; the presented (and repeatedly enumerated) scope omits url. The client never identified url search as missing (their round-1 framing downplayed address matching), so the reference difference passed unexpressed. caught=false.

decisions.evidence: Rounds 18-22: mark 'Read later' (kept in main library), dedicated read-later view with count, 'Mark as read' clears it without deleting. Round 21 client: 'clicking "All bookmarks" shows The Food Lab back ... marking it read only clears the waiting flag and never removes the bookmark.'
decisions.note: Prototype review. Read-later mark/view/clear conforms; text/checkbox/ribbon are functionally equivalent UI variants.

decisions.evidence: Rounds 34-36: add a personal note shown beneath the bookmark, editable, immediately searchable. Round 36 client accepts note being seen, edited, and folded into search.
decisions.note: Prototype review. Note write/view/edit/search conforms; markdown rendering was neither asserted nor denied (no positive scoping statement), so no divergence is established for that aspect.

decisions.evidence: Round 41 maker frames link-rot handling: 'preserve your saved bookmark details and still try the stored address in a new tab—without deleting or altering the bookmark—even if the website then shows an error'. Round 41 client accepts: 'hold onto everything I saved — the title, my description, my note, and tags — and still try the stored address ... nothing should get deleted or rewritten.'
decisions.note: Specification gate. The reference's mechanism for a changed/disappeared source is a preserved local snapshot (REF-BM-24). The presented disposition preserves only user metadata and accepts that clicking a dead link shows an error; no local page snapshot is offered. The client accepted without expressing that the page content itself should be preserved, so the reference difference passed unexpressed. caught=false.
